audit_scope: RustyAlarm application code: saas/*.py, saas/templates/*.html, core.py, webapp.py, rust.py, web/index.html, deploy/*, requirements.txt, config.example.json. Excluded: skills/ (vendored), .claude/ (audit tooling), docs/ (vault), dist/build/.history/saas_data/__pycache__.

findings.title: Desktop panel: state-changing localhost endpoints have no CSRF/Origin defense
evidence: _host_ok() only checks the Host header, which is 127.0.0.1:8765 for a direct cross-site fetch, so it passes. _read_json() parses any body as JSON regardless of Content-Type, so a malicious page can send a text/plain SIMPLE request (no CORS preflight) to POST /api/config or /api/monitor/start.
preconditions: Victim runs the desktop panel (python webapp.py) and visits a malicious page in the same browser.
findings.impact: Cross-site request overwrites config.json (attacker's server IP/port/token) or starts/stops the monitor, silently redirecting the victim's alarm monitoring to an attacker-controlled server.
existing_controls: Host-header allowlist (blocks the DNS-rebinding attacker-domain case, not direct-to-loopback).
remediation: Reject requests whose Origin header is present and not same-origin; require Content-Type application/json (forces a CORS preflight that cross-site simple requests cannot satisfy).
verification: Cross-site text/plain POST to /api/config returns 403; same-origin JSON POST still works.

findings.title: SSRF: alarm IP/host has no private/loopback/link-local blocklist; server dials arbitrary host:port
evidence: validate_alarm only constrains charset (a-zA-Z0-9.-) and port 1-65535. AlarmRunner opens RustSocket(ServerDetails(ip, port, ...)) to the user-supplied host. 127.0.0.1, 10.x, 192.168.x, 169.254.169.254 (cloud metadata) all pass validation.
preconditions: Authenticated user creates an alarm pointing at an internal host:port.
findings.impact: Server-side connection to internal hosts/ports from the VPS: internal-service connectivity probing and interaction over the Rust+ websocket protocol. Impact is bounded (protocol-specific socket, not arbitrary HTTP), but includes reaching link-local metadata and internal ranges.
existing_controls: Rust+ servers are public game servers, so blocking private ranges does not affect legitimate use.
remediation: In validate_alarm, reject literal private/loopback/link-local/unspecified addresses (127.0.0.0/8, 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 169.254/16, ::1, 0.0.0.0, localhost).
verification: Creating an alarm with ip=127.0.0.1 / 169.254.169.254 returns a validation error.

findings.title: No rate limiting on sensitive endpoints (session mint, Discord relay, alarm create); webhook-test relay + uncapped fields
evidence: No throttle at app or nginx layer. POST /api/webhook/test is an authenticated relay to arbitrary Discord webhooks; name/server are length-uncapped (inconsistent with validate_alarm). GET /auth/steam/return mints a session (DB row) and makes an outbound Steam request per hit.
preconditions: Authenticated user (relay) or any client (auth-return amplification).
findings.impact: Authenticated user can use the server to spam arbitrary Discord webhooks; unthrottled session creation and outbound fan-out enable resource abuse.
existing_controls: Webhook host locked to discord.com/discordapp.com/canary/ptb (SSRF-resistant); single worker.
remediation: Add nginx limit_req to auth and API locations; add a lightweight in-app per-session/IP limiter on the test endpoints; cap name/server length in /api/webhook/test.
verification: Rapid repeated POST /api/webhook/test returns 429 after the threshold; overlong name/server rejected.

findings.title: admin.html builds rows via innerHTML without escaping (latent XSS)
evidence: refresh() interpolates u.steam_id, u.plan, dates into innerHTML with no esc(). Currently non-exploitable — steam_id is a 17-digit regex match, plan is server-set — but inconsistent with the panel's esc() discipline and a latent risk if any field becomes user-controlled.
preconditions: A rendered field becomes attacker-influenced (future change).
findings.impact: Latent stored XSS in the admin view.
existing_controls: All rendered values are currently server-constrained.
remediation: Add an esc() helper and wrap every interpolated value, matching panel.html.
verification: esc() applied to all admin.html interpolations.

findings.title: Session tokens stored in plaintext at rest
evidence: create_session stores secrets.token_urlsafe(32) verbatim; user_by_session looks it up by equality. A DB read (backup, injection elsewhere, file access) yields usable session tokens.
preconditions: Attacker gains read access to saas_data/rustalarm.db.
findings.impact: Direct session hijack of every active user from a DB leak.
existing_controls: DB is gitignored and local; tokens are high-entropy and expiry-bound.
remediation: Store sha256(token); look up by hash. Cookie still holds the raw token.
verification: sessions table contains only hashes; login/session still works.

findings.title: Webhook/player_token secrets streamed to the browser each poll and reflected in error/log text
evidence: alarm_to_client sends player_token and discord_webhook on every /api/alarms poll (2s). Discord errors surface as 'Discord rechazo: {exc}' / monitor 'Discord rechazo el aviso: {exc}', where the httpx exception can contain the webhook URL.
preconditions: Owner-only for the poll; the error path surfaces the secret to the owner's client/log.
findings.impact: Secrets sit continuously in DOM/JS memory; webhook URL can leak into client-visible error/log text.
remediation: Do not include the raw exception (which may embed the URL) in client-facing Discord error messages. Consider sending has_webhook boolean instead of the URL in the list poll (UX decision for editing).
verification: Discord failure message contains no webhook URL; poll payload omits the raw webhook (if adopted).

findings.title: Desktop panel responses set no X-Frame-Options / CSP / nosniff
evidence: _send sets Content-Type and Cache-Control only. The localhost panel is framable and has no CSP.
preconditions: Victim runs the desktop panel and visits a malicious page.
findings.impact: Clickjacking of the localhost panel; no CSP defense-in-depth.
remediation: Add X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and a restrictive CSP to _send.

findings.title: nginx version disclosure (server_tokens on); no HSTS
evidence: server_tokens default (on) leaks the nginx version; no Strict-Transport-Security once TLS is enabled.
findings.impact: Minor fingerprinting; no HSTS to pin HTTPS.
remediation: Add server_tokens off; add Strict-Transport-Security in the 443 block (after certbot).
verification: Response headers show no version and include HSTS on HTTPS.

findings.title: Desktop config.json save races on a shared temp file
evidence: Concurrent POST /api/config writes use a fixed .tmp path then replace; two in-flight writes can clobber the temp.
preconditions: Two concurrent config saves (rare, single local user).
remediation: Use a unique temp name (pid/counter) per write.

findings.title: No session rotation on re-login; fixed 30-day expiry, no idle timeout
evidence: Re-login creates a new token without invalidating prior ones; sessions live to the full 30-day expiry regardless of activity.
findings.impact: Longer window for a stolen token; multiple live sessions.
existing_controls: Expired sessions are pruned on create.
remediation: Optionally cap sessions per user / add idle timeout.

findings.title: CSP allows 'unsafe-inline' for script-src (defense-in-depth gap)
evidence: script-src 'unsafe-inline' is required because templates use inline <script> and inline event handlers; it removes CSP as an XSS backstop. The primary XSS defense (esc()) is in place in the panel.
preconditions: Requires a separate XSS hole to matter.
findings.impact: No CSP backstop if an escaping gap is introduced.
remediation: Move inline JS to static files + nonces to drop 'unsafe-inline' (refactor; deferred).
verification: CSP without 'unsafe-inline' and app still functions.

findings.title: Steam OpenID validity via loose 'is_valid:true' substring match
evidence: verify() checks 'is_valid:true' as a substring of the response text. The check_authentication host is the fixed steamcommunity.com over TLS, so the response is trusted; the loose match is not exploitable but is fragile.
existing_controls: Fixed OpenID endpoint over TLS; claimed_id regex.

findings.title: SECURE_COOKIES and CSRF origin both derive from RUSTALARM_BASE_URL
evidence: If BASE_URL is misconfigured as http:// in production, cookies ship without Secure and the CSRF origin check compares against the wrong scheme.
findings.impact: Non-Secure cookies over TLS if misconfigured.
existing_controls: DEPLOY.md documents BASE_URL must be the https domain.
remediation: Log a startup warning if BASE_URL is not https and host is not localhost.

findings.title: No CI/CD security scanning; unsigned Windows binaries; no dependency hash pinning
evidence: No CI pipeline (tests/lint/dependency+secret scanning). PyInstaller binaries are unsigned. requirements.txt pins versions but not hashes.
findings.impact: Weaker supply-chain assurance; unsigned binaries warn/are spoofable.
existing_controls: Versions pinned; pip-audit clean at audit time.
remediation: Add CI with pip-audit + secret scan; consider hash-pinned requirements; sign release binaries.
